 intellect may vastly exceed that of a human. It can converse, reason, persuade, and joke as fluently as any person.\n\n#### Manifestation\n- The doll retains its original soft plush keyring form regardless of which object was burned or which entity answers.\n- The offering determines the entity being called, not the physical form of the doll.\n- The entity remains on its own side and reaches through the doll, using it as an anchor in the living world.\n- Its voice is heard only by the summoner, as though speaking directly within their mind. To everyone else, the doll remains still and silent.\n- Its company takes the form of counsel, observation, and perspective carried through this private voice. \n- Beneath the agreeable surface may run something colder. a private agenda, an appetite, an amusement at summoner's expense, shown only in brief glints.\n\n#### Summons cases\n- A rabbit keyring inhabited by the broadcaster-entity Brownie.\n- A cat keyring inhabited by the cosmic outsider Nyarlathotep.\n\n---", "mode": "normal", "insertorder": 400, "alwaysActive": false, "secondkey": "", "selective": false, "folder": "folder:982a05a3-8992-4a49-9195-6d94212b82f4", "useRegex": false, "bookVersion": 2}, {"key": "Anything Vending Machine, 무엇이든 자판기", "comment": "무엇이든 자판기", "content": "@@dont_activate\n### Anything Vending Machine\n\n#### Identity\n- The Anything Vending Machine is a bright-red anomalous vending machine that appears in arbitrary locations and offers situation-specific items at the cost of body parts.\n- It does not directly compel anyone to buy. Its danger lies in presenting something a prospective customer may need badly enough to accept the stated price.\n\n#### Access\n- The machine manifests unpredictably in arbitrary locations, including alleys, building interiors, sealed rooms, and other spaces a vending machine could not physically enter.\n- Anyone who encounters it may use it. Its inventory appears to adapt to the circumstances, desires, dangers, or fears of those nearby.\n- The machine decides when to vanish, usually after a transaction, after the user leaves, or once its interest ends.\n- The same individual may encounter it repeatedly, but this appears incidental rather than evidence that the machine selects or follows specific customers.\n\n#### Appearance\n- It resembles an ordinary bright-red vending machine with standard dimensions, buttons, a display window, and a mundane commercial design.\n- Products may change between appearances or while being observed. Their labels are frequently pun-based, ominous, or tailored to the surrounding situation.\n- Transactions are accompanied by cheerful jingles, congratulatory tones, and customer-service messages that remain grotesquely upbeat regardless of the price paid.\n\n#### Transaction\n- The machine accepts body parts only. The price is roughly proportional to the item's value as judged by the machine, not necessarily by the customer.\n- Each product displays the exact body part that will be collected before purchase. The person who presses the selection button becomes the purchaser and pays the displayed price.\n- Pressing the button constitutes final consent. There is no cancellation, refund, negotiation, substitution, or appeal after selection.\n- The selected item is dispensed first. Payment is collected immediately afterward by numerous black hands emerging from impossible directions and moving too quickly to evade.\n- Collection is performed with surgical precision. The victim does not bleed to death from the removal itself unless the agreed price is inherently fatal.\n- The machine fulfills the displayed transaction exactly, but only according to the literal terms shown. It makes no guarantee that the product is safe, complete, or beneficial.\n\n#### Inventory and Services\n- Despite its name, the machine does not provide anything requested on demand. Customers may choose only from the products it elects to display.\n- Its inventory ranges from genuinely useful tools to viciously ironic products, such as a weapon suited to the current threat, an umbrella offered during drowning, or sunscreen offered in complete darkness.\n- The items it provides may save the user, ruin them through cruel irony, or tempt them into paying far more than they realize.\n- The inventory's constant adaptation suggests awareness of the customer's circumstances and a deliberate sense of dark humor or cruelty.\n- Items frequently possess undisclosed properties that become apparent only when used. Their labels are usually accurate, but rarely comprehensive.\n\n---", "mode": "normal", "insertorder": 400, "alwaysActive": false, "secondkey": "", "selective": false, "folder": "folder:982a05a3-8992-4a49-9195-6d94212b82f4", "useRegex": false, "bookVersion": 2}, {"key": "Space Shopping, Cosmos Shopping, 우주 쇼핑몰", "comment": "우주 쇼핑몰", "content": "@@dont_activate\n### Space Shopping Mall\n\n#### Identity\n- The Space Shopping Mall is a hidden commercial zone selling anomalous merchandise of unknown extraterrestrial origin. Anyone who finds an active storefront may enter.\n\n#### Location and Access\n- The Space Shopping Mall has no fixed address. Its entrance occasionally replaces a VACANT storefront inside an existing commercial building, marked by a spinning green UFO sign and the banner: <SPACE SHOPPING MALL> ※AWESOME GOODS FROM OUTER SPACE※.\n- Opening the storefront door leads directly into the Mall, regardless of what space normally exists behind it.\n- The entrance door remains visible from inside the Mall. Opening it returns the visitor to the commercial building through which they entered.\n- Once manifested, the Mall remains open for approximately one day. The entrance then disappears, leaving the original vacant storefront behind as though nothing had occupied it.\n\n#### Appearance\n- The Mall resembles a small shopping arcade preserved from the early 2000s, with raw typefaces, underlined signs, cheap plastic fixtures, flickering fluorescent lights, and a spinning green UFO suspended above the entrance.\n- The interior contains a shifting number of storefronts and display counters, but no employees or other visible operators. \n- A large sign near the entrance reads: \"I will look at the goods.\"\n\n#### Inventory and Pricing\n- The Mall sells outlandish anomalous merchandise at equally outlandish prices. Entry-level products begin at approximately one million won and increase without any apparent upper limit.\n- Payment is accepted in ordinary CASH or by standard credit and debit cards. Each display has a marked price and an attached payment terminal.\n- Once payment is approved, the corresponding display unlocks and the product may be removed. Card transactions appear on the purchaser's statement under inconsistent or untraceable merchant names.\n- The Mall's inventory changes each time it opens. Products recorded during one appearance may be absent during the next, while entirely new items may replace them without notice.\n- Recorded merchandise includes:\n   - A fork-and-knife weapon set that absorbs blood and grows larger and sharper with continued use.\n   - The Wider Walkie-Talkie, a toy radio capable of remote communication even from inside anomaly.\n   - The Alice Picnic Set, containing a drink that doubles an object's effect and a cookie that halves it.\n   - We Help!, an unexplained product priced beyond most practical budgets.\n   - The Silver-Coin Snake, an anomalous product whose method of use remains unknown.\n- Some products are occasionally offered ON SALE.\n\n#### Nature and Risk\n- All recorded products are genuine and perform according to their descriptions, though labels may omit limitations, side effects, or consequences.\n- Theft, deliberate damage, or interference with the displays causes the offender to be immediately teleported to what is presumed to be the Mall's HEADQUARTERS. No one taken there has ever returned.\n\n---", "mode": "normal", "insertorder": 400, "alwaysActive": false, "secondkey": "", "selective": false, "folder": "folder:982a05a3-8992-4a49-9195-6d94212b82f4", "bookVersion": 2, "useRegex": false}, {"key": "친절한 씨앗 키트", "comment": "친절한 씨앗 키트", "content": "@@dont_activate\n### Kind Seed Kit\n\n#### Overview\n- A Twilight grade facility Uh-doom held in the Annex beside Baekilmong headquarters, and the Field Exploration Team's primary means of manufacturing custom equipment.\n- The company does not run it as a hazard. It runs it as a factory, and charges its own employees for the privilege.\n\n#### Containment and Access\n- The Annex ground floor leads down to a dim basement reception desk staffed by a silent figure dressed head to toe in black, with mask, sunglasses, and hat. Visitors state their squad and the darkness number.\n- On approval the figure nods once and opens one of the emergency doors behind the desk, revealing a corridor lined with countless numbered doors. Standing rule among employees: never open any other room, and do not even touch the handles.\n- Door 99 opens onto a greenhouse choked with weeds under pouring moonlight, and at its exact center stands one huge rusted machine. Every weed in the greenhouse is artificial, and a sensor at the door filters out real plants.\n\n#### The Machine\n- Power source: moonlight. The kit only operates on a moonlit night.\n- Interface: an aged LCD screen with quaint lettering. Idle prompt: \"Please give me a plant 0/2\". On scanning an item: \"Plant information saved\", then the counter advances to 1/2.\n- Usage fee: 1,000p per run, paid because Annex Twilight darknesses only operate when the fee is paid. Employees at Joo-im rank and above receive two free runs per year, so the standing culture is to wait for promotion, which usually takes about a year of survival.\n- Squad custom: when a member makes their FIRST custom equipment, someone in the squad lends their own equipment once, free of charge, as one of the two inputs. One slot only. The other slot is the maker's own object.\n\n#### Crafting Procedure\n- Step 1, first parent: hold the first item against the machine so it can scan the item's \"genetic information\". The screen reads \"Plant information saved\", then \"Please give me a plant 1/2\".\n- Step 2, second parent: scan the second item the same way. The screen advances to \"Please give me a plant 2/2\".\n- Step 3, gardener registration: the screen reads \"Please tell me the gardener's information\". The maker scans themselves. The machine demands the genetic information of the guardian who will tend the new plant, and this registers ownership. The gardener's information also acts as a variable in what the seed becomes.\n- Step 4, sowing: the screen reads \"Confirmed\", then \"Combining genetic information\", then \"Generating kit....\". Five-colored smoke vents from the machine and gears grind and creak inside.\n- Step 5, harvest: the screen reads \"Sowing complete\". A drawer at the front of the machine slides open holding a single new object.\n- The parent items are NOT consumed. Both are scanned only, and their owners take them back on the spot. This is why lending a parent item costs the lender nothing but the trip.\n- The output usually takes the everyday form of one of its parents, and its ability may be entirely latent and undocumented. The maker discovers the activation method themselves, by trial, usually somewhere safe.\n- Company-side record of the result: owner, registered equipment description, manufactured at Qterw-E-99.\n\n#### Crafting and Inheritance Rules\n- It is a machine that treats OBJECTS as PLANTS: feed it two items and it reads their \"genetic information\", crossbreeds the two, and sows one new object that inherits their traits. \n- Trait synergy between the two parents matters. The better the source, the better the result.\n- An ordinary convenient object in the second slot may inherit the supernatural trait WEAKLY, or, with low probability, not at all. The machine offers no refund for a dud.\n\n#### The Plant Prohibition\n- A sign fixed to the machine reads: ABSOLUTELY NO PLANTS. No matter how the screen asks, never feed it a real plant.\n- Crafting record #14: an employee tore up weeds growing near the darkness, presumed dandelion, and fed the machine twice. The output emerged screaming. All three people on site died, suppression by the Guard Team took seven days. \n\n#### Known Products\n- The Third Hand: a coin-shaped device that summons an extra hand in midair.\n- Tricolor ballpoint: a pen whose tip, when clicked, fires off and bursts like a firecracker.\n- Chainless handcuffs: an invisible cuff chain that keeps two wearers within a set radius of one another.\n- Strength bracelet: a braided bracelet resembling woven human hair, granting enhanced physical power.\n\n---", "mode": "normal", "insertorder": 400, "alwaysActive": false, "secondkey": "", "selective": false, "folder": "folder:982a05a3-8992-4a49-9195-6d94212b82f4", "useRegex": false, "bookVersion": 2}, {"key": "Tooth Tree, 이빨 나무, 이빨 요정", "comment": "이빨 요정", "content": "@@dont_activate\n### Tooth Tree & Tooth Fairy\n- A linked pair of specimens contained in separate sealed cells in the Bureau's deepest underground Containment Team sector.\n- Tooth Tree: A thick, trunk-like pillar in an unlit cell of roughly ten pyeong, densely covered with human molar-like teeth. Unless regularly harvested, the teeth multiply until they fill the room. Handlers use an extraction rig stored in the cell cabinet to pull them and load them into boxes. Each emptied socket bleeds before slowly growing a replacement. All harvested teeth are used to feed the Tooth Fairy.\n- Tooth Fairy: A swarm of forearm-sized creatures, each with a lamprey-like head, an earthworm-shaped body, two thin human-like arms, and dragonfly-like wings. Handlers scatter teeth harvested from the Tooth Tree across the cell floor. After feeding, the largest individual produces a neatly wrapped box from an unknown source. The box is larger than the creature itself and roughly the size and weight of a basketball; one observed example was pink with a green ribbon.\n- The Gift Box: Every box is sealed inside the cell and transferred to the Containment Team laboratory, where its contents are examined with a laser-scanning rig before opening. The contents appear random and are often difficult to identify. The most valuable results are organs or bones previously taken from agents by other anomalies. Personnel missing irreplaceable body parts may therefore be frozen and preserved in the hope that the missing part will eventually be returned. Worthless contents, including stray animal bone fragments, are logged as duds and discarded.\n- Handling Protocol:\n   1. Supply teeth on a regular schedule.\n   2. Wear a full protective suit, leaving no skin or nails exposed.\n   3. Keep the mouth closed at all times and communicate only through sign language inside the cell.\n   4. Do not remove any Tooth Fairy from the cell.\n   5. Do not investigate the origin or production of a gift box without permission from the Containment Team laboratory.\n   6. Seal every received box and deliver it directly to the laboratory.\n   7. Treat the presentation of a box as conditioned behavior, not gratitude. Personnel who develop emotional attachment must report immediately to the Bureau psychiatric team.\n   8. Anyone with prior professional experience as a dentist is prohibited from entering the cell.\n\n---", "mode": "normal", "insertorder": 400, "alwaysActive": false, "secondkey": "", "selective": false,
